name: Roman
summary_description: One of the most influential civilizations in history, Rome evolved from a small city-state on the Tiber River to a vast empire spanning three continents. Roman culture shaped law, governance, architecture, engineering, and language across Europe and beyond.

name: Ancient Greek
summary_description: The cradle of Western philosophy, democracy, and the arts. Greek city-states like Athens and Sparta developed distinctive political systems, produced enduring works of literature and philosophy, and made foundational contributions to mathematics, science, and theater.

name: Sumerian
summary_description: The earliest known civilization, Sumerians invented writing (cuneiform), developed complex irrigation, built ziggurats, and established the first cities. Their innovations in mathematics, astronomy, and law influenced all subsequent Mesopotamian civilizations.

name: Ancient Egyptian
summary_description: One of the longest-lasting civilizations in history, ancient Egypt was defined by the Nile River, monumental architecture, a complex religious system centered on the afterlife, and a sophisticated hieroglyphic writing system. Egyptian innovations in medicine, engineering, and art influenced the entire ancient world.

name: Han Dynasty Chinese
summary_description: The Han Dynasty represents one of the golden ages of Chinese civilization. It established Confucianism as state ideology, expanded the Silk Road trade network, invented paper, and developed advanced iron smelting. The Han ethnic identity and cultural norms established during this period continue to shape Chinese civilization.

name: Aztec
summary_description: The Aztec Empire was the last great Mesoamerican civilization, centered on the island city of Tenochtitlan. Known for sophisticated agriculture (chinampas), monumental temple architecture, complex social hierarchy, and a powerful military. Their calendar system and religious practices reflected deep astronomical knowledge.

name: Viking
summary_description: Seafaring Norse warriors, traders, and explorers who expanded across Europe, the North Atlantic, and even North America. Viking culture combined a warrior ethos with sophisticated craftsmanship, oral literary traditions (sagas and eddas), and a rich mythological system centered on the Aesir gods.

name: Inca
summary_description: The largest empire in pre-Columbian America, stretching along the Andes from Colombia to Chile. The Inca built an extensive road network, developed sophisticated agricultural terracing, and administered their empire without writing through the quipu knot-record system. Their architectural masonry remains among the most precise in history.

name: Maya
summary_description: One of the most intellectually advanced civilizations of the ancient world, the Maya developed a fully phonetic writing system, a vigesimal mathematical system including the concept of zero, and highly accurate astronomical calendars. Their city-states featured towering pyramid temples, elaborate palace complexes, and sophisticated water management.

name: Mughal
summary_description: The Mughal Empire brought together Persian, Central Asian, and Indian cultural traditions to create one of the most magnificent civilizations in history. Known for architectural masterpieces like the Taj Mahal, a flourishing of miniature painting, and the synthesis of Hindu and Islamic artistic traditions.
